verses.text: Elisha had told the woman whose son he had brought back to life, "Get up and leave with your family. Go and stay wherever you can, because the LORD has called for a famine. It will come on this land for seven years."
So the woman got up and did what the man of God said. She and her family went and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
At the end of the seven years, she came back from the land of the Philistines. She went to the king to ask him to give back her house and her land.
At that moment the king was talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God. He said, "Tell me about all the great things Elisha has done."

Just as Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman whose son it was came in to ask the king for her house and her land. Gehazi said, "My master the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life."

The king asked the woman about it, and she told him. Then the king gave her an official and said, "Give back everything that belonged to her, including all the crops her land produced from the day she left until now."
Elisha went to Damascus. Ben-Hadad king of Syria was sick. When the king was told, "The man of God has come here,"
he said to Hazael, "Take a gift with you and go meet the man of God. Ask the LORD through him, 'Will I get better from this sickness?'"

So Hazael went to meet Elisha. He took a gift of all the best things from Damascus, loaded on forty camels. He came and stood in front of him and said, "Your son Ben-Hadad king of Syria has sent me to ask, 'Will I get better from this sickness?'"
Elisha said to him, "Go and tell him, 'You will surely get better.' But the LORD has shown me that he will surely die."
Elisha stared at Hazael until Hazael felt uncomfortable. Then the man of God began to cry.

Hazael asked, "Why are you crying, my master?" Elisha answered, "Because I know the harm you will do to the Israelites. You will set their forts on fire, kill their young men with the sword, smash their little children to death, and rip open their pregnant women."
Hazael said, "How could your servant, who is only a dog, do such a great thing?" Elisha answered, "The LORD has shown me that you will become king of Syria."
Then Hazael left Elisha and went back to his master. Ben-Hadad asked him, "What did Elisha tell you?" Hazael answered, "He told me you would surely get better."
But the next day, Hazael took a thick cloth, soaked it in water, and spread it over the king's face until he died. Then Hazael became king in his place.
In the fifth year that Joram son of Ahab was king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat began to rule as king of Judah.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, as Ahab's family had done, because he married Ahab's daughter. He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes.
But for the sake of his servant David, the LORD did not want to destroy Judah. He had promised to give David and his descendants a lamp forever.
While Jehoram was king, Edom rebelled against Judah's rule and chose its own king.
So Jehoram went to Zair with all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, but he got up at night and attacked them, and his army ran home to their tents.
So Edom has been free from Judah's rule to this day. The town of Libnah rebelled at the same time.
The rest of what Jehoram did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
Jehoram died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. His son Ahaziah became king after him.
In the twelfth year that Joram son of Ahab was king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram began to rule as king of Judah.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for one year. His mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.
He followed the ways of Ahab's family and did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, as Ahab's family had done, because he was related to Ahab's family by marriage.
Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead. The Syrians wounded Joram.

So King Joram went back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Syrians had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. Then Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because he had been wounded.
